name: Ochra, or Gumbo
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: beef, cut into small pieces
ingredients.originalText: 2 lbs. of beef, cut into small pieces

ingredients.name: ½ lb. corned ham or pork, also cut up
ingredients.originalText: ½ lb. corned ham or pork, also cut up

instructions.text: Put the meat and ochras together in a pot with a quart of cold water—just enough to cover them—and let them stew for an hour.
Then add the tomatoes and two quarts of boiling water—more, if the liquid in the pot has boiled away so as to expose the meat and vegetables.
Boil three-quarters of an hour longer, skimming often with a silver spoon.
When the contents of the vessel are boiled to pieces, put in the butter, with cayenne pepper and salt, if the ham has not seasoned it sufficiently.
Strain and send up with squares of light, crisp toast floating upon it.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put the meat and ochras together in a pot with a quart of cold water—just enough to cover them—and let them stew for an hour.
2. Then add the tomatoes and two quarts of boiling water—more, if the liquid in the pot has boiled away so as to expose the meat and vegetables.
3. Boil three-quarters of an hour longer, skimming often with a silver spoon.
4. When the contents of the vessel are boiled to pieces, put in the butter, with cayenne pepper and salt, if the ham has not seasoned it sufficiently.
5. Strain and send up with squares of light, crisp toast floating upon it.
